transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-24 15:00 UTC (48m)
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jorge Ramos, Ida Chen (Redwood); Lena Ortiz, Rajiv Menon, Hannah Cole, Tom Park (BlueAurora)
Recording note: partial audio drop ~00:37-00:45; some words auto-corrected.

Summary: quick check-in focused on staging access, rehearsing failover paths (regional + canary fallback), and conditioning traffic to exercise KV caching and batch impacts. Confirmed readiness gaps: staging creds, KMS rotation windows, and one firewall rule for egress to Redwood dedicated nodes. Agreed next steps to run a scripted failover rehearsal.

Topics covered: onboarding status; failover rehearsal plan; traffic shaping script; KV cache priming; SSO/KMS windows; acceptance criteria for POC success.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey, everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the pilot. Jorge from SE will take the tech bits. Ida will track action items.
[00:18] Lena: hey, Lena here, platform owner for BlueAurora. quick morning for me.
[00:22] Rajiv: Rajiv, ML infra. we'll want to push the failure modes today.
[00:26] Tom: Tom, SRE.
[00:28] Hannah: Hannah, security ops.
[00:30] Jorge: great, thanks. Agenda: check staging access, walk through the failover rehearsal, traffic shaping, and any security windows.
[00:40] Maya: quick perf note — last week's bench showed the 8k context model at median 140ms token on hosted, but when we batch at 8 the p95 stretched. so rehearsal will exercise that.
[01:03] Rajiv: right, and we also saw the KV cache miss rate go up when prefixes weren't primed, that bit was weird — is that KV cache consistent between dedicated and hosted?
[01:15] Jorge: good question. so the runtime maintains prefix/KV caching differently depending on route — in hosted we use prefix caching that persists per token-window, in dedicated you can pin cache policy. sometimes the transcriber has been saying like K V k cache — but yeah it's the same concept.
[01:36] Hannah: on the security side we need to know when you plan key rotations — our KMS rotations could break long-running sessions if they collide.
[01:45] Maya: noted. Hannah, can you share the rotation window?
[01:50] Hannah: sure, typical window is Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC but we can lock a no-rotate window if needed. I'll confirm blackout.
[02:02] Lena: staging creds — last pass we gave a user with too-broad roles, Tom had to rollback. we want least-privilege roles for the rehearsal.
[02:12] Tom: yeah pls don't give full admin. we only need the minimal IAM to call the staging endpoint and SSH to the bastion for logs.
[02:22] Jorge: for the rehearsal script we'll need an API key, a staging endpoint, and one ephemeral role for the traffic generator.
[02:30] Rajiv: also we want to simulate region failover — route primary us-west, fail to eu-west, then fallback to a lower-capacity variant. can Redwood flip routing automatically?
[02:44] Jorge: yes, our smart routing has a policy you can set: prefer region, then cost-tier fallback. for the rehearsal we'll set an aggressive health-check threshold so we trigger the fallback during the scripted outage.
[02:58] Maya: quick aside — are there any regulatory egress rules? we've got customers who need data residency.
[03:05] Lena: BlueAurora keeps PII in-region; the pilot uses synthetic data so fine. just documenting.
[03:11] Rajiv: ok. next, traffic shaping — Jorge, walk through the script.
[03:20] Jorge: sure. plan is: 1) ramp to 100 qps with small payloads for 3 mins, 2) spike to 500 qps for 90s to exercise circuit breakers, 3) sustained 50 qps with long-context prompts to hit KV cache miss/hit cycles. we'll provide sample prompts.
[03:45] Jorge: note: the script will also include a 'prefix prime' phase to warm the KV cache so you can see the delta when we flush.
[03:55] Rajiv: flushing cache is important — can we time the flush to coincide with failover so we see both at once?
[04:01] Jorge: yes, during the rehearsal we'll trigger a cache invalidation via the admin API (we'll give you a temporary token).
[04:09] Hannah: admin API token — we need audit logs and a TTL. can we scope the token and have it expire automatically?
[04:15] Jorge: token TTL supported; we'll hand back a scoped token that only permits cache:invalidate and read logs.
[04:22] Tom: firewall note — one of our egress rules blocks outbound to the dedicated node IP range. we'll need that opened.
[04:28] Lena: yeah, we flagged that last week but it wasn't updated. Rajiv, can you add the rule?
[04:33] Rajiv: I'll add it after the call, it'll take ops 20 minutes to propagate.
[04:38] [00:45] (audio glitch — 7s)
[04:45] Maya: okay, Sabrina — sorry, that was the glitch — moving on. acceptance criteria for the rehearsal?
[04:53] Tom: SRE wants <200ms median token latency at 50 qps sustained and failover complete within 30s for region switch.
[05:02] Jorge: and from product side we want no more than 2% increase in hallucination rate post-failover for the test prompts — we'll run a quick eval set.
[05:10] Lena: security: zero unauthorized KMS access and full audit logs captured for the admin actions.
[05:16] Hannah: we'll sample logs and confirm SSO sessions didn't drop unexpectedly.
[05:21] Maya: good. tech deep-dive: Rajiv raised a weird throughput plateau at 300qps during last bench — Jorge, any guesses?
[05:30] Jorge: likely queue saturation in the batcher — if requests have wide length variance the batcher can form inefficient batches. we'll instrument the batch histogram and add adaptive batch windows.
[05:40] Rajiv: can we turn off batching for the spike phase? we'd like to see raw per-request latencies.
[05:46] Jorge: yes, we'll provide a config flag to set batch size = 1 for spike testing. keep in mind cost and token billing change.
[05:55] Tom: also, can Redwood stream logs to our SIEM in near real-time? last time there was a few minute lag.
[06:03] Jorge: we have an event-streaming route to push traces and token-level metrics; we can set it to low-latency mode for the rehearsal. that will increase events volume.
[06:12] Hannah: please note retention policy — we require 90-day retention for audit events. any shortfalls here?
[06:18] Jorge: hosted default is 30 days, enterprise add-on supports 90. for the pilot we can temporarily extend retention for the rehearsal window.
[06:27] Maya: costs aside, we'll note that as a requirement if they want to go to Dedicated/Private.
[06:33] Lena: one more infra frag — the staging deploy had an older quant profile; inference quality dipped by 3% on the eval. Rajiv, can you confirm which model variant we should use?
[06:43] Rajiv: we want v2-quant-a, it's the tradeoff point between latency and quality. please pin that during the rehearsal.
[06:50] Jorge: noted — we'll pin v2-quant-a and include a fallback to v2-quant-b if capacity constrained.
[06:57] Maya: ok. logistic — Jorge will share the scripted runbook link, Maya will schedule the rehearsal, Rajiv will provide creds. can we pick a window next Wed?
[07:07] Lena: works for us in the morning PT.
[07:10] Tom: morning PT good.
[07:12] Hannah: I'll confirm KMS blackout.
[07:15] Maya: perfect. any blockers?
[07:18] Rajiv: just the staging IAM role scope and the firewall rule; I'll action both tonight.
[07:23] Jorge: I'll post the traffic-shaper and the sample prompts; note that prompts include a few placeholder proper nouns that the transcriber may mangle — we'll label them clearly in the doc.
[07:33] Lena: also, can we get an export of the last bench CSV and the p95/p99 traces? that'll help correlate.
[07:40] Jorge: yes, I'll add the bench CSV to the pilot folder. link: https://redwood.ai/pilot/blueaurora/benchmarks (internal)
[07:50] [00:08] Ida: capturing action items and sending meeting notes after.
[07:55] Maya: quick Q from Rajiv earlier — can we simulate KMS rotation mid-session to see session resilience?
[08:02] Hannah: we can, but we'd want to coordinate a narrow window; do not do production keys obviously.
[08:08] Tom: agree, only staging keys.
[08:12] Maya: ok, add simulated KMS rotation to the rehearsal checklist.
[08:16] Jorge: we'll add cache invalidation, region fail, KMS rotation, and a short network partition to the script.
[08:23] Rajiv: perfect.
[08:26] Maya: great, wrap up — recap next steps and owners.
[08:30] Ida: I'll email notes and attach the runbook once Jorge posts it.
[08:34] Maya: thanks all, we'll reconvene after the rehearsal for a debrief.
[08:39] Lena: thanks.
[08:40] Meeting adjourned.
